correctness.rationale: Path contraction preserves weighted spanning-tree counts. The matrix-tree cofactor has a rank-one explicit determinant, giving the probability for every prescribed simple path, with empty outside parts included. Marked-path disjointness, falling-factorial enumeration and telescoping prove both exact finite tails for every admissible a,b,k. Summing log survival factors with k on the scale sqrt(ab/(a+b)) establishes the Rayleigh tail when both parts diverge. Actual packaged verify.py passed 83,789 exact assertions; finite checks are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Exact finite bipartite parity-specific two-point distance tails were not located in primary literature read or semantic result searches. Burton–Pemantle gives a general edge-inclusion method, Alappattu–Pitman a complete-graph birthday law, and Archer–Shalev a dense-graph scaling result. The explicit all-size falling-factorial evaluation and both endpoint classes are not stated in inspected sources; residual priority risks are acknowledged.
residual_risks: A previously published explicit complete-bipartite loop-erased walk path distribution was not located; failure of search does not rule it out.
Burton–Pemantle general transfer-impedance determinants can be specialized to the path law, potentially reducing perceived novelty.
Rayleigh asymptotics for balanced bipartite graphs are covered in principle by broader CRT results and are not claimed independently original.

value.rationale: A finite explicit survival law for distances of two fixed vertices in a uniform spanning tree of K_{a,b} is a motivated intrinsic metric invariant, not an artificial restriction: it determines exact distance quantiles for both endpoint geometries. Two different parity-resolved product laws remain valid even in strongly asymmetric finite graphs, and yield an all-ratios Rayleigh limit without invoking dense-graph scaling theorems. These sharp finite expressions are not implied numerically by previously stated general asymptotic results.
